details:
**Confessions of a Mask** – Mishima’s semi‑autobiographical novel in which the narrator, “Kochan,” struggles with his homosexuality and attempts to hide it behind a façade of conformity.

**The Temple of the Golden Pavilion** – A novel about the Buddhist monk Mizoguchi who, driven by aesthetic obsession and personal turmoil, sets fire to the famous Kinkaku‑ji temple.

**Sea of Fertility tetralogy** – Mishima’s four‑book series (Spring Snow, Runaway Horses, The Temple of Dawn, The Decay of the Angel) that follows Judge Shigekuni Honda’s quest to identify the reincarnations of his friend Kiyoaki through distinctive birthmarks.

**Shigekuni Honda** – The retired judge who appears in the Sea of Fertility novels; he believes a trio of moles on a young man’s back signals a past‑life connection to Kiyoaki Matsugae.

**Kiyoaki Matsugae** – Protagonist of Spring Snow, whose three moles become the key identifier for Honda’s search for the soul’s rebirth across the tetralogy.

**Mizoguchi (the monk)** – Central figure of The Temple of the Golden Pavilion; his inner conflict and aesthetic ideals culminate in the arson of the temple he tends.

**“When you meet the Buddha, kill the Buddha”** – A Zen koan quoted in Mishima’s works that inspires Mizoguchi (and other characters) to destroy the Buddhist temple, symbolizing a rejection of spiritual authority.

**1970 public seppuku after a failed coup** – Mishima’s dramatic ritual suicide on live television following the abortive attempt to restore political power to the Japanese emperor.

**Sun and Steel** – Mishima’s autobiographical essay describing his bodybuilding regimen, the visceral experience of slicing an apple on a ship, and his philosophy that the body must be honed like steel.

**My Friend Hitler** – A controversial play written (and reportedly performed) by Mishima in which he portrayed Adolf Hitler, reflecting his fascination with extreme nationalist and authoritarian figures.

**Guido Reni’s St. Sebastian painting** – Frequently referenced in Mishima’s narratives; characters obsessed with the image of a beautiful, dying young man, underscoring themes of aestheticism and mortality.

**Kashiwagi (the club‑footed student)** – A recurring character who uses his clubfoot to elicit sympathy from women; appears in The Temple of the Golden Pavilion and other stories.

**Kochan’s attraction to Omi and inability to love Sonoko** – A plot thread in Confessions of a Mask illustrating the protagonist’s homosexual desire for the male character Omi and his failure to form a conventional heterosexual relationship with Sonoko.

**Reincarnation identified by three moles** – A motif throughout the Sea of Fertility series where characters’ birthmarks serve as evidence of a soul’s successive lives, driving Honda’s obsessive investigations.

**The Sailor Who Fell From Grace with the Sea** – One of Mishima’s early novels, featuring the storm‑driven episode where the protagonist proves his worth by securing a ship’s mooring buoy to win the hand of the shipowner’s daughter; also introduces themes of youthful idealism and tragedy.
